name: Qijianglong
sum: Qijianglong is a long-necked mamenchisaurid known from a partial skeleton with a skull from the Suining Formation of China.
wsnote: The holotype was about 15 m long (cited Wikipedia revision).
holotype: QJGPM 1001, a partial skeleton with the rear of the skull, a partial lower jaw, all seventeen neck vertebrae, the first six back vertebrae, ribs, 28 rear tail vertebrae and part of the limbs.
biology: It had a long neck of seventeen vertebrae.
author: Xing et al. 2015

sources.text: L. Xing, T. Miyashita, and J. Zhang, D. Li, Y. Te, T. Sekiya, F. Wang, P. J. Currie. 2015. A new sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic of China and the diversity, distribution, and relationships of mamenchisaurids. Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 35(1):e889701:1-17
Paleobiology Database — taxon and occurrence records for Qijianglong (downloaded 2026-11-21).

dates_note: The Suining Formation is of debated age, Late Jurassic or Early Cretaceous by different methods; PBDB gives Oxfordian–Tithonian.
